export.readme.android:
# {name}: Android and iOS app

This project is your site inside a native app made with [Capacitor](https://capacitorjs.com/docs) (version 8).
The site is in `www/`; `capacitor.config.json` holds the name (`{name}`) and the identifier (`{id}`).

## What to install once

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22 or newer.
- For Android: [Android Studio](https://developer.android.com/studio).
- For iPhone: a Mac with Xcode.

## Build the Android app

```sh
npm install
npx cap add android
npx @capacitor/assets generate --android
npx cap open android
```

In Android Studio, use **Build › Generate Signed App Bundle / APK** to build the `.aab` (Google Play) or the `.apk`
(installed straight on the phone).

## Build the iPhone app

```sh
npx cap add ios
npx @capacitor/assets generate --ios
npx cap open ios
```

In Xcode, choose your team under *Signing & Capabilities* and use **Product › Archive** to send it to the App Store.

## Update the app after changing the site

Export again, replace the `www/` folder with the new one and run `npx cap sync`.

## Before publishing: your app's identifier

The stores know the app by `appId` in `capacitor.config.json` (now `{id}`). Change it to one of your own
before the first upload, a domain of yours read backwards (`com.yourcompany.yourapp`: lowercase letters and digits
only in each part), and keep it from then on: a build under another identifier installs as another app, not as an
update.

## Change the icon

The app's icons are made from `assets/icon-only.png` (the start page's favicon, or the site's initial on its colour) by
[@capacitor/assets](https://capacitorjs.com/docs/guides/splash-screens-and-icons), in the steps above. Replace that
file with your own 1024 × 1024 PNG and run `npx @capacitor/assets generate` again. The files in `www/icons/` are the
icons of the site installed from the browser, not of this app.

## Another option: publish on the Play Store without Android Studio

Publish the site (the editor's Publish button) and paste its address into [PWABuilder](https://www.pwabuilder.com): it
builds the Android package (TWA) straight from the published site.
export.readme.desktop:
# {name}: app for Windows, macOS and Linux

This project is your site inside a desktop app made with [Electron](https://www.electronjs.org) and packaged by
[Electron Forge](https://www.electronforge.io). The site is in `app/`; `main.js` opens the window, and links to
other sites, e-mail addresses and phone numbers open in the computer's own apps.

The icons are in `build/` (`icon.ico` for Windows, `icon.icns` for macOS, `icon.png` for Linux): replace them with
your own, keeping the names, before building the installer.

## What to install once

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.13 or newer.

## Try it

```sh
npm install
npm start
```

## Build the installer

```sh
npm run make
```

The result is in `out/make/`:

- on Windows: `squirrel.windows/…/{name} Setup.exe`, the installer;
- on macOS: a `.zip` with the `.app`;
- on Linux: a `.deb` and a `.zip`.

Each system builds its own installer: run `npm run make` on Windows to get the `.exe`.

## Update the app after changing the site

Export again, replace the `app/` folder with the new one and run `npm run make`.

## Another option: the Microsoft Store without installing anything

Publish the site (the editor's Publish button) and paste its address into [PWABuilder](https://www.pwabuilder.com): it
builds the Microsoft Store MSIX package straight from the published site. The published site also installs from Edge or
Chrome (the *Install app* icon in the address bar), because it already is an installable app (PWA).
